p.src: It happened that the elderly Imperial Consort mentioned in the previous chapter had died, and all titled ladies were required to attend court in their appointed ranks and observe mourning according to their degree. An imperial edict proclaimed throughout the realm that for one year no titled household might hold banquets or make music, while commoners were forbidden to marry for three months. The Lady Dowager, Ladies Xing, Wang, You, and Xu, mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law, grandmothers and granddaughters alike, went to court every day to attend the rites and did not return until after the middle of the afternoon. After the coffin had lain for twenty-one days in a side palace within the imperial precincts, the spirit was to be escorted to the ancestral mausoleum, in a place called Xiaoci County. The mausoleum lay some ten days’ round journey from the capital; once the coffin arrived, it would remain there several more days before being placed in the underground chamber, so the whole affair would take about a month. Jia Zhen and his wife of the Ning mansion naturally had to go as well. With no masters left in either mansion, the family conferred and, since the household lacked anyone in charge, reported that Lady You had recently given birth, thereby excusing her from attendance and freeing her to help manage affairs in both the Rong and Ning mansions. They also asked Aunt Xue to stay in the Garden and look after the young ladies and their maids. Aunt Xue therefore had no choice but to move into the Garden. Baochai already had Xiangyun and Xiangling staying with her; although Aunt Li and her daughter had for the moment left Li Wan’s quarters, they might return at any time for three or five days, and the Lady Dowager had also placed Baoqin in Li Wan’s care; Yingchun had Xiuyan with her; Tanchun was burdened with household affairs and was frequently disturbed by Aunt Zhao and Jia Huan, making her quarters most unsuitable; and Xichun’s rooms were too cramped. Moreover, the Lady Dowager had repeatedly and earnestly charged Aunt Xue to care for Lin Daiyu. Aunt Xue had always been especially fond of her, and now that circumstances provided the opportunity, she moved into the Xiaoxiang Lodge to share Daiyu’s rooms, taking the greatest care over all her medicines, food, and drink. Daiyu was boundlessly grateful. From then on, she followed Baochai’s manner of address: even in Baochai’s presence she called Aunt Xue simply “Mother,” called Baochai “elder sister,” and Baoqin “younger sister.” They seemed born of the same parents and were more intimate than any of the others. Seeing this, the Lady Dowager was greatly pleased and set her mind at ease. Aunt Xue confined herself to caring for the girls and keeping their maids in order; she would not interfere in any of the household’s affairs, great or small. Although Lady You came over every day, she did little more than appear and answer the roll, and she too was unwilling to wield authority capriciously. Besides, she alone remained to manage everything in her own household, and each day she also had to see that the Lady Dowager’s and Lady Wang’s lodgings were supplied with all the necessary food, drink, furnishings, and bedding, so she was greatly overworked.

p.src: Thus, with the masters of both the Rong and Ning mansions so fully occupied, their stewards too were in confusion: some had accompanied them to court, some were attending to the lodgings outside the palace, and others had gone ahead to prepare those lodgings. Consequently, the servants of both houses were left without proper direction and began to shirk their duties; some formed factions when opportunity offered and joined the temporary officeholders in secretly abusing their authority. Only Lai Da and a few managers remained in the Rong mansion to oversee external affairs. Several men whom Lai Da ordinarily relied upon had already gone away. Though he appointed others in their place, they were all inexperienced, and he found them awkward to use. Moreover, in their ignorance, some cheated people without restraint, some lodged accusations without evidence, and some recommended men without cause. All manner of misconduct bred trouble everywhere—too much to recount in full.

p.src: They also observed that every official household maintaining actors or actresses was releasing and dismissing them all. Lady You and the others therefore agreed to report the matter to Lady Wang when she returned and release their twelve young actresses as well. Yet someone remarked, “These girls were bought in the first place. Even if they no longer study singing, we could perfectly well keep them as servants and let only their instructors go.” Lady Wang said, “Girls trained for the stage are not the same as ordinary servants. They too were daughters of respectable families, but poverty forced their people to sell them into this calling, where for several years they have had to paint their faces and play all manner of grotesque roles. Now that this opportunity has arisen, we had better give each of them a few taels for traveling expenses and let them go their own ways. Our ancestors followed this precedent in their day. If we were to keep them now, we would be impairing our hidden virtue and showing ourselves petty besides. It is true that a few of the older women are still here, but each had her own reason for refusing to go home. That was why they remained in service and, when they grew older, were married to young men of our household.” Lady You said, “Then we shall ask all twelve of them. Those who wish to go home can send word to their parents, who must come in person to take them back; we shall give each girl a few taels for the journey. That will be the safest course. If we do not require their parents or relatives to come, some scoundrel may assume a false name, claim a girl, and sell her again; then all this benevolence would have been wasted. Any who do not wish to leave can remain.” Lady Wang smiled and said, “That is a sound proposal.” Lady You and the others also sent someone to inform Xifeng. Meanwhile, instructions were sent to the administrative office that each instructor was to receive eight taels of silver and be free to go wherever she pleased. Every item in the Pear Fragrance Court was checked, entered in the register, and taken into custody, and men were assigned to keep watch at night. When the twelve girls were summoned and questioned face to face, more than half proved unwilling to return home. Some said that, though their parents were alive, they thought of nothing but selling their daughters and would merely sell them again if they went back. Some had lost their parents or had been sold by uncles, elder brothers, or younger brothers. Some said they had no one to turn to, while others could not bear to leave those who had shown them kindness. Only four or five wished to leave. When Lady Wang heard this, she had no choice but to let the others remain. The four or five who wished to leave were sent home with their foster-mothers to wait until their own parents came to claim them, while those unwilling to go were distributed throughout the Garden as servants. The Lady Dowager retained Wenguan for her own service. She assigned Fangguan, who played principal female roles, to Baoyu; sent Ruiguan, who played young female roles, to Baochai; assigned Ouguan, who played young male roles, to Daiyu; sent Kuiguan, who played leading painted-face roles, to Xiangyun; sent Douguan, who played secondary painted-face roles, to Baoqin; and sent Aiguan, who played elderly male roles, to Tanchun. Lady You asked to take Qieguan, who played elderly female roles. Thus each found her proper place. Like weary birds released from their cages, they played in the Garden every day. Everyone knew that they could not sew and were unaccustomed to domestic service, so no one reproved them severely.

p.src: One day, when a grand sacrifice was being held at court, Grandmother Jia and the others set out at the fifth watch. They first went to their temporary quarters for some refreshments and light food, then entered the palace. When the early-morning ceremony was over, they withdrew to their quarters and ate breakfast. After resting briefly, they returned to court and waited until the midday and evening sacrifices had ended; only then did they leave for their quarters, rest, eat supper, and return home. As it happened, these quarters were in the family temple of a high official, where Buddhist nuns pursued their devotions; it had a great many rooms, all exceedingly clean. There were eastern and western courtyards: the Rong mansion rented the eastern one, while the Prince of Beijing's household rented the western one. The Dowager Princess and the young Princess rested there each day. Seeing that Grandmother Jia and her party were in the eastern courtyard, the two households went in and out together and could look after one another. There is no need to recount the minor details of affairs outside the household.

p.src: Now, in Prospect Garden, Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang were away from home every day and would not return from accompanying the funeral procession for a month. The maids and old serving women therefore had time on their hands and often amused themselves in the garden. Moreover, all the old serving women who had attended the performers in Pear-Fragrance Court were withdrawn and dispersed through the garden for general service, making it seem as though the garden had gained several dozen more people. Wenguan and the others were, some of them, proud by nature; some bullied their inferiors by relying on powerful patrons; some were fussy about clothes and food; and some had sharp, quarrelsome tongues. On the whole, many of them were unruly and unreasonable. Consequently, not one of the old serving women was without resentment, though none dared argue openly with them. Now that the troupe had been disbanded, everyone had got her wish. Some simply washed their hands of the matter, while others, being narrow-minded, still nursed old grudges. But since all the girls had been assigned to the various apartments, the women did not dare come and harass them.

p.src: As it happened, that day was the Qingming Festival. Jia Lian had prepared the customary annual offerings and took Jia Huan, Jia Cong, and Jia Lan to Iron Threshold Temple to sacrifice before the coffins and burn paper offerings. Jia Rong of the Ning mansion likewise went with several members of the clan, each having prepared sacrificial offerings. Baoyu had not yet fully recovered, so he was unable to go. After his meal he grew drowsy, and Xiren said, "The weather is lovely. Go out for a little stroll. You shouldn't fall asleep the moment you put down your bowl of congee, or the food will lie heavy on your stomach." At this, Baoyu had no choice but to take a walking stick, slip his feet into his shoes, and step out of the courtyard. Recently the garden had been divided among the old serving women to manage, each with her own task, and everyone was busy: some tending bamboo, some attending to trees, some planting flowers, and some sowing beans. In the pond, women boatmen were poling boats about, scooping up mud and planting lotus roots. Xiangling, Xiangyun, Baoqin, and their maids were all seated on the rocks, watching the workers for amusement. Baoyu came slowly toward them. Seeing him approach, Xiangyun hurriedly laughed and called, "Push that boat out quickly! They've come to fetch Cousin Lin!" Everyone burst out laughing. Baoyu flushed, but he too laughed and said, "When someone is ill, we all mean her well. Yet you turn it into a joke and make fun of her." Xiangyun laughed. "Even the way she's ill is different from everyone else and invites laughter. Yet here you are finding fault with me!" As they spoke, Baoyu sat down too and watched the bustle for a while. Then Xiangyun said, "It's windy here, and the rocks are cold too. You should go inside and sit down."

p.src: Baoyu had in fact been meaning to visit Lin Daiyu, so he rose, took up his stick, said goodbye to them, and followed the embankment by Drenched-Fragrance Bridge. He saw willows trailing golden threads and peach trees breathing crimson clouds. Behind some rocks stood a great apricot tree whose blossoms had all fallen; its foliage was dense and richly green, and many little apricots the size of beans had already formed among the leaves. Baoyu thought, "I was ill for only a few days, yet I have missed the apricot blossoms entirely! Before I knew it, 'green leaves have spread their shade, and fruit hangs thick upon the boughs'!" He therefore gazed up at the apricots, unable to tear himself away. Then he remembered that Xing Xiuyan's husband had already been chosen. Though marriage was one of the great affairs of life for men and women and could not be avoided, it still meant that there would be one fewer lovely girl among them. In no more than two years, she too would have 'green leaves spreading their shade, and fruit hanging thick upon the boughs.' In a few more days the apricots would fall and leave the branches bare; in a few more years, Xiuyan's black hair would inevitably turn silver and her rosy beauty wither. The thought saddened him, and he could only weep and sigh before the apricot tree. As he stood there grieving and sighing, a sparrow suddenly flew down, alighted on a branch, and began chirping wildly. Baoyu fell once more into one of his foolish reveries and thought, "This sparrow must have visited when the apricot blossoms were in full bloom. Now it sees no flowers, only fruit and leaves, and so it too cries in distress. Its notes must surely be sounds of weeping. What a pity Gongye Chang is not here before me, for then I could ask him. But when the tree blossoms again next year, will this sparrow still remember to fly back here and meet the apricot flowers once more?"

p.src: While his thoughts were running wild, he suddenly saw a flare of fire beyond the rockery, startling the sparrows into flight. Baoyu was greatly startled. Then he heard someone over there shouting, “Ouguan, are you trying to get yourself killed? How dare you bring spirit money in here and burn it? I’ll go back and report you to the mistresses—they’ll have your hide for this!” More puzzled than ever, Baoyu hurried around the rockery to look. There was Ouguan, her face streaked with tears, crouching on the ground with a flame still in her hand, grieving over a heap of spirit-money ashes. Baoyu hastily asked, “For whom are you burning spirit money? Quickly, stop burning it here. If it is for your parents or brothers, tell me their names. I’ll have the pages outside prepare a parcel, write the names on it, and burn it for you.” At the sight of Baoyu, Ouguan said not a word. Baoyu questioned her repeatedly, but she would not answer. Suddenly an old woman came striding up viciously and seized Ouguan, saying, “I’ve already reported you to the mistresses, and they’re beside themselves with anger.” At this, Ouguan’s childishness got the better of her. Afraid of being humiliated and losing face, she refused to go. The old woman said, “I warned you not to get too carried away. You cannot carry on here as freely as you did outside. This is a place where every inch is governed by rules.” Pointing at Baoyu, she continued, “Even our young master observes the rules. Who do you think you are, coming here to make trouble? Being frightened won’t save you. Come with me at once!” Baoyu hurriedly said, “She wasn’t burning spirit money at all. Cousin Lin sent her here to burn some spoiled sheets of writing. You failed to look carefully and reported her by mistake.” Ouguan had been at a complete loss, and the sight of Baoyu had only added to her fear. But when she suddenly heard him covering for her, her anxiety turned to joy. Plucking up her courage, she said defiantly, “Did you really see clearly that it was spirit money? What I burned was paper on which Miss Lin had spoiled her writing!” Hearing this, the old woman grew still more spiteful. She bent down and searched the ashes for scraps that had not completely burned, picked up two fragments, and said, “Still talking tough, are you? Here is the proof and the evidence. We’ll settle this before the mistresses in the hall!” With that, she seized Ouguan by the sleeve and tried to drag her away. Baoyu quickly caught hold of Ouguan and knocked the old woman’s hand away with his walking stick. “Go ahead and take that scrap back with you,” he said. I’ll tell you the truth. Last night I had a dream in which the Spirit of the Apricot Blossom asked me for a string of white spirit money. She said no one from my own rooms was to burn it; if a stranger burned it for me, my illness would mend more quickly. So I obtained this white spirit money and went especially to ask Cousin Lin to trouble Ouguan to come and burn it for me while offering the proper invocation. No one was supposed to know about it. That is why I was finally able to get up today—yet you had to see it. Now I feel ill again, all because you disrupted the rite! And you still mean to report her.

Ouguan had been at a complete loss, and the sight of Baoyu had only added to her fear. But when she suddenly heard him covering for her, her anxiety turned to joy. Plucking up her courage, she said defiantly, “Did you really see clearly that it was spirit money?
What I burned was paper on which Miss Lin had spoiled her writing!”

Hearing this, the old woman grew still more spiteful. She bent down and searched the ashes for scraps that had not completely burned, picked up two fragments, and said, “Still talking tough, are you? Here is the proof and the evidence.
We’ll settle this before the mistresses in the hall!”
With that, she seized Ouguan by the sleeve and tried to drag her away.
Baoyu quickly caught hold of Ouguan and knocked the old woman’s hand away with his walking stick. “Go ahead and take that scrap back with you,” he said.

I’ll tell you the truth. Last night I had a dream in which the Spirit of the Apricot Blossom asked me for a string of white spirit money. She said no one from my own rooms was to burn it; if a stranger burned it for me, my illness would mend more quickly.
So I obtained this white spirit money and went especially to ask Cousin Lin to trouble Ouguan to come and burn it for me while offering the proper invocation.
No one was supposed to know about it. That is why I was finally able to get up today—yet you had to see it.
Now I feel ill again, all because you disrupted the rite!
And you still mean to report her.

p.src: Ouguan, go with her. When you see the mistresses, just repeat exactly what I have said. When the Old Lady returns, I shall tell her that this woman deliberately offended the deity so that it would bless me with an early death.” This gave Ouguan still more confidence, and she now took hold of the old woman and tried to pull her away instead. Alarmed by these words, the old woman hastily dropped the spirit money and appealed to Baoyu with an ingratiating smile. “I truly knew nothing about it. If Second Master reports me to the Old Lady, won’t that be the end of this old woman? I’ll go back to the mistresses now and say that the young master was making an offering to a deity and that I mistook what I saw.” Baoyu said, “You must not go back to them at all. If you do not, I shall say nothing.” The old woman replied, “But I have already made my report, and they sent me to bring her in. How can I possibly not go back? Well then, I’ll say that I found her, but Miss Lin summoned her away.” Baoyu considered this for a moment before nodding his consent. The old woman had no choice but to leave.

p.src: Baoyu then asked Ouguan, “For whom were you really burning that spirit money? If it were for your parents or brothers, I imagine you would already have asked someone to burn it outside for you. Since you burned these few sheets here, there must be some private reason behind it.” Ouguan was deeply grateful for the way he had just protected her and realized that he was a kindred spirit. With tears in her eyes, she said, “Apart from Fangguan in your rooms and Ruiguan, who serves Miss Bao, not a third person knows about this matter of mine. Now that you have happened upon me and shown me such kindness, I can hardly avoid telling you too. But you must never speak of it to anyone else.” Then, weeping again, she said, “I cannot very well tell you face-to-face. Go back and ask Fangguan quietly when no one else is present, and you will understand.” Having said this, she composed herself as if nothing had happened and went away.

p.src: Baoyu was perplexed by what he had heard. With nothing else to be done, he strolled over to the Naiad’s House, where Daiyu looked pitiably thinner than ever, though when he asked after her health, he learned that she was considered much recovered compared with before. Daiyu saw that he too had grown much thinner than before. Remembering what had happened in earlier days, she could not keep from shedding tears. After they had spoken together for a little while, she urged Baoyu to go and rest so that he might regain his strength. Baoyu had no choice but to return. He was intent on asking Fangguan the whole story, but Xiangyun and Xiangling happened to be there, chatting and laughing with Xiren and Fangguan. He could not conveniently call Fangguan aside, for fear that the others would question him again, so he had no choice but to curb his impatience.

p.src: Presently Fangguan went with her foster mother to wash her hair. But her foster mother deliberately had her own daughter wash first and made Fangguan wait until afterward. Seeing this partiality, Fangguan said, “You expect me to wash in the water left over by your daughter. You keep all my monthly allowance and profit at my expense, yet you still give me nothing but leftovers.” Her foster mother’s shame turned to anger, and she cursed her: “You ungrateful little wretch! No wonder everyone says actors are impossible to deal with. However decent a person may be, joining that profession ruins them. A filthy little brat like you, picking faults and spouting foul nonsense, like a mule that bites the rest of the herd!” Thus foster mother and daughter began to quarrel. Xiren hurriedly sent someone to tell them, “Stop that racket! The Old Lady has scarcely left the house before none of you can speak a quiet word.” Qingwen remarked, “It is all Fangguan’s fault for not knowing how to behave. She has gone quite wild. Just because she knows a couple of operas, she acts as if she had slain the king of the bandits and captured all the rebels.” Xiren said, “One hand alone cannot clap. The older one is much too unfair, but the younger one is much too provoking as well.” Baoyu said, “Fangguan is not to blame. As the old saying goes, ‘Injustice makes its protest heard.’ She has lost her family and relations, and there is no one here to look after her, while they pocket the money she earns. And then they mistreat her besides—how can anyone blame her?” Then he asked Xiren, “How much does she receive each month? Why not take charge of it yourself from now on and look after her? Would that not save trouble?” Xiren replied, “If I mean to look after her, am I not already doing so? Must I take those few coins of hers before I will care for her? That would only invite people’s abuse.” As she spoke, she rose and went into the other room, where she fetched a bottle of scented hair oil, some eggs, soap, hair cords, and the like. She summoned an old servant woman to take them to Fangguan and tell her to fetch fresh water and wash her own hair instead of quarrelling. Her foster mother felt still more ashamed and accused Fangguan of being “heartless, making up lies that I have withheld your money.” She struck Fangguan several times, and Fangguan began to cry. Baoyu started outside, but Xiren hastily stopped him. “What are you doing? I will go and speak to her.” Qingwen hurried there first, pointed at Fangguan’s foster mother, and said, “At your age, you truly ought to know better. You would not provide what she needed to wash her hair, so we gave it to her; instead of feeling ashamed, you still have the face to strike her. If she were still at the school learning her art, would you dare strike her then?” The old woman replied, “Call a woman mother for one day, and she is your mother for life. If she puts on airs with me, I have every right to beat her!” Xiren called to Sheyue, “I am no good at quarrelling, and Qingwen is too hot-tempered. Go over quickly and frighten her with a few stern words.” Hearing this, Sheyue hurried over and said, “Stop shouting for a moment.

p.src: Let me ask you this: never mind our quarters—look throughout the whole garden. Who has ever presumed to discipline a daughter assigned to a master’s household? Even if she were your own daughter, once she had been assigned to separate quarters and had a master, her master would have the right to beat or scold her, as would the senior maids and young ladies. Who gave her parents leave to interfere halfway through? If all of you interfere like this, what are the girls supposed to learn by serving us? The older you grow, the less you seem to understand the rules! Did you see Zhuier’s mother come and make a scene the other day and decide to imitate her? Do not imagine you are safe. I have not reported you only because one person after another has been ill these past few days and the Old Lady has had no peace of mind. Once things quiet down in a day or two, we shall make a full report and have all your arrogance thoroughly curbed. Baoyu has only just begun to recover, and even we dare not speak loudly, yet you beat someone until her screams fill the place. The mistresses have been away for only a few days, and already you behave as if no law binds you and hold us in no regard. Give it another two days, and you will be beating us next. If she chooses not to have you as her foster mother, do you think she will be left buried in dung and straw?” Furious, Baoyu struck the threshold with his walking stick and said, “It is truly astonishing that these old women should all have hearts of iron and bowels of stone. They cannot care for the girls and instead torment them. If this continues indefinitely, what is to become of them?” Qingwen said, “What do you mean, ‘What is to become of them?’ Drive the whole lot out! We have no use for these people who look capable but are good for nothing!” The old woman was overwhelmed with shame and said not a word. Fangguan wore only a crab-apple-red padded jacket and silk trousers patterned with scattered flowers, their cuffs hanging loose. Her glossy black hair streamed down her back, and she was drenched in tears. Sheyue laughed. “They have taken a young lady Yingying and turned her into Hongniang under torture! And now you will not dress yourself either, but remain so loose and untidy.” Baoyu said, “She looks excellent just as she naturally is. Do not truss her up too tightly.” Qingwen went over and took her by the hand, washed her hair clean, and wrung it dry with a towel. She loosely twisted it into an indolent coiffure, then told Fangguan to dress and come over to their quarters.

p.src: Next, a woman from the inner kitchen came and asked, “Supper is ready. Shall we bring it in?” Hearing this, a young maid went inside to ask Xiren. Xiren laughed. “We were making such a commotion just now that I never noticed how many times the clock struck.” Qingwen said, “Something must be wrong with that wretched thing again. We’ll have to see to it.” As she spoke, she took up the watch, looked at it, and said, “Just wait about half the time it takes to drink a cup of tea.” The young maid went away. Sheyue laughed. “Speaking of mischief, Fangguan deserves a few strokes herself. Yesterday she fiddled with that pendant, and before half a day had passed it was broken.” While they talked, they made the tableware ready. Presently a young maid came in carrying a food box and stood waiting. When Qingwen and Sheyue opened it, they found the same four small side dishes as before. Qingwen laughed. “Now that he’s recovered, couldn’t they give him a couple of light dishes? How long are they going to keep up this business of rice gruel and pickles?” As she laid out the meal, she looked into the box again and discovered a bowl of fresh bamboo-shoot soup with ham, which she hastily set before Baoyu. Baoyu bent over the table and took a sip. “It’s scalding!” he said. Xiren laughed. “Merciful Buddha! You’ve gone without meat for only a few days, yet look how ravenous you are.” As she spoke, she quickly picked up the bowl and blew gently over it. Seeing Fangguan beside her, she handed it to her and said with a smile, “You should learn how to wait on your master too, instead of always acting foolish and sleeping like a log. Blow lightly, and mind you don’t spray spittle into it.” Fangguan did as she was told and blew several times, quite properly.

p.src: Her godmother, meanwhile, was waiting outside the door with the meal. When Fangguan and the other actresses had first arrived, each had been assigned a godmother from among the outside servants, and the women had accompanied them to Pear-Fragrance Court. These nominal godmothers had originally been third-rank servants in the Rong mansion. They had merely been charged with washing and mending for the girls and had never served in the inner apartments, so they knew nothing of its rules. It was only through the girls’ good fortune that they had now gained entry to the Garden and could follow their goddaughters to their rooms. This woman had already been put in her place once by Sheyue and had learned a little of the rules. Afraid that Fangguan might be forbidden to acknowledge her as godmother, which would cost her many advantages, she was intent on winning them over. Now, seeing Fangguan blowing on the soup, she hurried inside and said with a smile, “She’s inexperienced and may break the bowl. Let me blow on it.” As she spoke, she reached out to take it. Qingwen called out at once, “Get out! Even if she smashed the bowl, it still wouldn’t be your place to blow on the soup. Who gave you leave to come barging into a place like this? Get out this instant!” Then she scolded the young maids. “Have you all lost your wits? She may not know the rules, but couldn’t you have told her?” The young maids all protested, “We tried to drive her out, but she wouldn’t go. We warned her, but she wouldn’t believe us. Now you’ve got us scolded because of you. Do you believe us at last? Of all the places we’re allowed to go, you may enter only half; the other half is still forbidden to you. Yet you not only came running into a place even we aren’t allowed to enter—you had to reach out your hands and put your mouth to things as well!” As they spoke, they pushed her outside. Several women waiting below the steps for the empty food boxes laughed when they saw her emerge. “Sister, you might at least have looked at yourself in a mirror before going in there!” The woman was so humiliated that she was both furious and resentful, but she could only swallow her feelings.

p.src: After Fangguan had blown on it several times, Baoyu smiled and said, “That’s enough. You’ll hurt your breath. Take a sip and see whether it’s cool enough.” Fangguan supposed he was teasing and merely smiled at Xiren and the others. Xiren said, “There’s no harm in taking a sip.” Qingwen laughed. “Watch me taste it.” With that, she took a sip. Seeing this, Fangguan took a sip herself and said, “It’s ready now.” She handed the bowl to Baoyu. Baoyu drank half the bowl, ate a few slices of bamboo shoot, and then half a bowl of rice gruel; that was all he wanted. The attendants cleared everything away and went out. A young maid brought in a washbasin, and when Baoyu had finished washing and rinsing his mouth, Xiren and the others went out to eat. Baoyu gave Fangguan a meaningful glance. Quick-witted by nature and trained for several years on the stage, how could she fail to understand? She therefore pretended to have a headache and said she would not eat. Xiren said, “Since you aren’t going to eat, stay here and keep him company. I’ll leave this gruel for you, and you can have it later if you get hungry.” With that, they all left.

p.src: Now that Baoyu and Fangguan were alone, he told her the whole story in detail: how it had begun with the light of the fire, how he had found Ouguan, how he had lied to protect her, and how Ouguan had asked him to question Fangguan. He then asked whom Ouguan had actually been making the offering to. Fangguan listened with a smile spreading over her face, then sighed and said, “The story is both amusing and sad.” On hearing this, Baoyu eagerly asked what she meant. Fangguan laughed. “Whom do you suppose she was making the offering to? It was for the dead Diguan.” “That was an act of friendship,” said Baoyu. “It was only right.” “Friendship indeed!” Fangguan said with a laugh. “It is a perfectly mad and foolish notion of hers. She says that she played the young male lead and Diguan the young woman, so they were often husband and wife onstage. Though it was only make-believe, all the words and actions they performed each day were those of genuine tenderness and loving consideration. The two of them became so carried away that even when they were not acting, in their ordinary meals and daily life, they behaved like a pair of devoted lovers. “When Diguan died, Ouguan wept until she nearly died herself. She has never forgotten her to this day, and so she burns paper offerings at every seasonal festival. “Later, Ruiguan was brought in to take Diguan’s place. When we saw Ouguan treating her with the same tenderness and consideration, we asked whether she had cast off the old love upon finding a new one. “She replied, ‘There is a great principle behind that too. “‘Suppose a man loses his wife: if circumstances require him to marry again, then remarrying is the proper thing to do. “‘So long as he does not cast the dead woman from his mind and cease to speak of her, he has shown that his love and devotion run deep. “‘But if, solely because she is dead, he refuses to remarry and lives alone all his life, thereby hindering a greater duty, that is unreasonable; the dead woman herself would find no peace.’ “Would you not call that both mad and foolish? “Is it not laughable when you hear it?” When Baoyu heard this foolish discourse, it accorded perfectly with his own foolish nature. He could not help feeling at once delighted and sorrowful; marvelling at it and praising it beyond measure, he said, “Since Heaven has created such a person, what need is there for a foul, bearded creature like me to defile the world?” Then he hurriedly took Fangguan by the hand and charged her, “Since that is how matters stand, I too have something I want you to tell her. It would be rather awkward for me to speak to her face-to-face, so you must convey it for me.” Fangguan asked what it was. Baoyu said, “From now on, she must never burn paper money again. “Paper money is a heterodox invention of later generations, not a teaching handed down by Confucius. “Whenever a season or festival comes around, she need only prepare a single burner and, on the appointed day, offer incense as she pleases. u.src: Now that Baoyu and Fangguan were alone, he told her the whole story in detail: how it had begun with the light of the fire, how he had found Ouguan, how he had lied to protect her, and how Ouguan had asked him to question Fangguan. He then asked whom Ouguan had actually been making the offering to.
Fangguan listened with a smile spreading over her face, then sighed and said, “The story is both amusing and sad.”
On hearing this, Baoyu eagerly asked what she meant.
Fangguan laughed. “Whom do you suppose she was making the offering to?
It was for the dead Diguan.”
“That was an act of friendship,” said Baoyu. “It was only right.”
“Friendship indeed!” Fangguan said with a laugh.

“It is a perfectly mad and foolish notion of hers. She says that she played the young male lead and Diguan the young woman, so they were often husband and wife onstage. Though it was only make-believe, all the words and actions they performed each day were those of genuine tenderness and loving consideration. The two of them became so carried away that even when they were not acting, in their ordinary meals and daily life, they behaved like a pair of devoted lovers.
“When Diguan died, Ouguan wept until she nearly died herself. She has never forgotten her to this day, and so she burns paper offerings at every seasonal festival.

“Later, Ruiguan was brought in to take Diguan’s place. When we saw Ouguan treating her with the same tenderness and consideration, we asked whether she had cast off the old love upon finding a new one.
“She replied, ‘There is a great principle behind that too.
“‘Suppose a man loses his wife: if circumstances require him to marry again, then remarrying is the proper thing to do.
“‘So long as he does not cast the dead woman from his mind and cease to speak of her, he has shown that his love and devotion run deep.
“‘But if, solely because she is dead, he refuses to remarry and lives alone all his life, thereby hindering a greater duty, that is unreasonable; the dead woman herself would find no peace.’
“Would you not call that both mad and foolish?
“Is it not laughable when you hear it?”

When Baoyu heard this foolish discourse, it accorded perfectly with his own foolish nature. He could not help feeling at once delighted and sorrowful; marvelling at it and praising it beyond measure, he said, “Since Heaven has created such a person, what need is there for a foul, bearded creature like me to defile the world?”

Then he hurriedly took Fangguan by the hand and charged her, “Since that is how matters stand, I too have something I want you to tell her. It would be rather awkward for me to speak to her face-to-face, so you must convey it for me.”
Fangguan asked what it was.
Baoyu said, “From now on, she must never burn paper money again.
“Paper money is a heterodox invention of later generations, not a teaching handed down by Confucius.

“Whenever a season or festival comes around, she need only prepare a single burner and, on the appointed day, offer incense as she pleases. If she does so with wholehearted sincerity and reverence, her devotion will reach the spirit.
“Foolish people do not understand this. Whether worshipping gods, Buddhas, or the dead, they insist on dividing them into ranks and prescribing a different form for each.
“They fail to realize that the two words ‘sincere heart’ are all that truly matters.

“Even in a time of panic and displacement, when not so much as a stick of incense is at hand, any earth or grass will serve as an offering provided it is clean. Not only will the dead receive it; gods and spirits will accept it too.
“Look at my own table: I keep only a single burner there and often offer incense without regard to the date.

p.src: “None of them knows why, but in my heart each offering has its own purpose. “If there is clear tea, I offer a cup of tea; if there is fresh water, a bowl of water. There may be fresh flowers or fruit, or even meat broth and fish dishes: so long as the heart is sincere and the intention pure, even a Buddha may come and partake of them. That is why reverence alone matters, not empty names and forms. “Tell her at once that she is never to burn paper again.” Fangguan listened and promised that she would. u.src: “None of them knows why, but in my heart each offering has its own purpose.

“If there is clear tea, I offer a cup of tea; if there is fresh water, a bowl of water. There may be fresh flowers or fruit, or even meat broth and fish dishes: so long as the heart is sincere and the intention pure, even a Buddha may come and partake of them. That is why reverence alone matters, not empty names and forms.
“Tell her at once that she is never to burn paper again.”
Fangguan listened and promised that she would.
After they had finished their meal, someone came to report, “The Old Lady and Her Ladyship have returned.”
To learn what followed, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
